4. Favorable local Davies rates can be represented explicitly

There is a genuine hardware-law freedom available within the stipulated one-site-Pauli bath.

Suppose stabilizer checks have weight at most  $w_{\mathrm{check}}$ , and each site belongs to at most  $q$  checks. Color the graph of overlapping checks with

 $C=w_{\mathrm{check}}(q-1)+1$ colors, and assign strengths

 $J_c=3^{c-(C-1)},\qquad c=0,\ldots,C-1.$ All strengths lie in a fixed positive interval independent of system size.

For a one-site Pauli  $P$ , its anticommuting checks have distinct colors. In the convention  $H=-\sum_jJ_jS_j$ , the energy change is

 $\Delta_P
=
2\sum_{c\in A(P)}J_c\sigma_c.$ Distinct sign patterns yield distinct frequencies. Subtracting two such expressions reduces to uniqueness of balanced ternary digits. Their separation is at least

 $4\,3^{-(C-1)}.$ A Davies rate function for that Pauli can therefore realize any selected positive rate table on these anticommuting-check patterns provided detailed balance is obeyed. This introduces no nonlocal controller or multiqubit bath coupling.

It remains a mathematical native-law construction. A physical claim would still need the declared spectral response and calibration warranty.

Why this does not yet provide error removal

The construction eliminates genuine zero-energy syndrome motion. Every syndrome-changing transition has energy magnitude at least

 $\delta_E=2\,3^{-(C-1)}.$ At formal zero temperature, a trajectory starting with energy  $E_0$  can make at most  $E_0/\delta_E$  downhill syndrome changes. At finite temperature,

 $\delta_E\,N_{\downarrow}
\le
E_0+\sum_{\text{uphill jumps}}\Delta E.$ This bounds work done by the dynamics, not the time needed to erase defects.

A four-qubit example shows the distinction exactly:

 $H=
-Z_1Z_2-\frac13Z_2Z_3
-Z_3Z_4-\frac13Z_4Z_1.$ In the computational configuration  $++--$ , both weak bonds are violated and both strong bonds are satisfied. Every syndrome-changing  $X$  or  $Y$  move raises energy by

 $2\left(1-\frac13\right)=\frac43.$ It is a strict non-ground local minimum despite the resolved, nonzero frequencies. Choosing favorable positive rates cannot turn its uphill edges into downhill ones.
